question: Asked to carry one of two buckets to the end of an alley, why did people pick up the nearer one and carry it further?
answer: To get something done sooner. Rosenbaum, Gong and Potts called it pre-crastination: hurrying to complete a step, even at extra physical cost. Their reading was that finishing a step frees the mind from having to hold it. Answering the quick email before starting the hard report is the same move.
move: Notice when you finish easy steps first just to stop holding them.
ask: Which easy task do I rush to tick off first, and what harder one does it push back?
source: Rosenbaum, Gong and Potts, Psychological Science, 2014
reference: Rosenbaum, Gong and Potts, Pre-crastination: Hastening subgoal completion at the expense of extra physical effort, Psychological Science, 2014
